prerequisites: It is advisable to possess the knowledge of Mathematics and Physics taught in scientific-technological baccalaureate.
It is advisable to have taken the course Physics I.

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire the necessary knowledge about the theoretical foundations and problem-solving techniques of Physics in the branches related to elementary Field theory, Electricity, and Magnetism.
Understanding and interpretation of texts and data, development of skills for their concretization and clear and succinct exposition.
Aptitude for the distribution of resources and time and their implementation in real situations.
Ability to transmit concepts, ideas, processes, etc., related to Industrial Engineering orally and in writing, clearly and correctly.
Ability to use scientific-technical tools for solving calculation and design problems in Industrial Engineering and aptitude for finding sustainable engineering solutions.
Ability to work together and ability to develop multidisciplinary projects.
Ability to relate to other people and open attitude towards creating new relationships.
Ability to incorporate new knowledge in the area of Industrial Engineering, based on acquired training and necessary for the evolution of technology.
Development of autonomy and creativity capacities, enhancing aptitudes for developing own initiatives and undertaking new projects.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts about the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism, and their application to solve engineering problems.

syllabus_topics: Practical laboratory sessions studying simple physical phenomena related to the theoretical program of the course.
